# Candidates flipped seven Senate seats this election. The winners are all on Substack.


### From governors’ races to House districts, a look at how candidates in both parties used Substack to speak directly to their constituents, plus tips for 2028


Nov 07, 2026


Illustration by Joro Chen, brand designer at Substack


In Tuesday’s momentous midterm elections, all seven Democrats who flipped Republican-held Senate seats—


[James Talarico](https://open.substack.com/users/157008787-james-talarico?utm_source=mentions)


in Texas, former Sen.


[Sherrod Brown](https://open.substack.com/users/114209545-sherrod-brown?utm_source=mentions)


in Ohio, former Gov.


[Roy Cooper](https://open.substack.com/users/391374123-roy-cooper?utm_source=mentions)


in North Carolina,


[Josh Turek](https://open.substack.com/users/381349194-josh-turek?utm_source=mentions)


in Iowa,


[Troy Jackson](https://open.substack.com/users/532006382-troy-jackson?utm_source=mentions)


in Maine, Dr.


[Annie Andrews](https://open.substack.com/users/246708914-annie-andrews?utm_source=mentions)


in South Carolina, and Rev.


[Adam Hamilton](https://adamhamiltonks.substack.com/) in Kansas—ran a Substack publication during the race. Two Senate races remain too close to call, and both challengers also have Substacks:


[Mary Peltola](https://open.substack.com/pub/marypeltola)


in Alaska and


[Scott Colom](https://substack.com/@colomforsenate) in Mississippi.


But the Senate races were only one slice of what happened across Substack this election cycle, with officeholders and candidates up and down the ballot writing, posting, going live, and filming videos for voters. In Texas, Gov.


[Greg Abbott](https://substack.com/@abbottcampaign?utm_source=about-page) and his challenger—now Governor-elect—


[Gina Hinojosa](https://open.substack.com/users/436345063-gina-hinojosa?utm_source=mentions)


, each published on Substack throughout their campaigns. In the U.S. House, Missouri’s


[Fred Wellman](https://open.substack.com/users/6517847-fred-wellman?utm_source=mentions)


won his race despite being outspent roughly 3 to 1 by the seven-term incumbent. The first-time candidate and 22-year Army veteran announced his run on Substack with a post titled “


[It’s official...I’m in!](https://substack.com/@fpwellman/p-189036058) ” His post after winning the nomination was similarly to the point: “


[Well, we won](https://fpwellman.substack.com/p/well-we-won) .”


Fred Wellman shared photos from the campaign trail on Substack.


Beyond the ballot, politicians used Substack to connect directly with their constituents. The


[State Department](https://substack.com/@statedept?utm_source=about-page) has published Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s op-eds on Substack, while Michigan Gov.


[Gretchen Whitmer](https://open.substack.com/users/446285196-gretchen-whitmer?utm_source=mentions)


has posted videos of conversations with


[New Mexico Gov.-elect Deb Haaland](https://gretchenwhitmer.substack.com/p/live-with-deb-haaland-and-gretchen) ,


[Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand](https://gretchenwhitmer.substack.com/p/my-conversation-with-rob-sand-17f) and others. Rep.


[Elise Stefanik](https://open.substack.com/users/489483862-elise-stefanik?utm_source=mentions)


published her


[personal reflection](https://elisestefanik.substack.com/p/25-years-since-911-never-forget) on the 25th anniversary of 9/11. Former Senate candidate


[Mallory McMorrow](https://open.substack.com/users/38768474-mallory-mcmorrow?utm_source=mentions)


, a Michigan state senator, started a podcast,


*[In the Arena](https://mallorymcmorrow.substack.com/podcast)* , where she interviewed state legislative candidates facing re-election in November. After the attempted assassination of President Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in April,


[Sen. Mark Kelly](https://open.substack.com/users/391424767-sen-mark-kelly?utm_source=mentions)


—whose wife, former Rep. Gabby Giffords, survived an assassination attempt in 2011—shared


[his thoughts](https://senmarkkellyaz.substack.com/p/political-violence-gun-violence-and) on gun violence in America.


Substack’s politics team has helped candidates determine the most meaningful ways to use the platform. “Politicians can access voters on every device at any time, but most of it is just noise,” says


[Cara Koontz](https://open.substack.com/users/31941223-cara-koontz?utm_source=mentions)


, who works with politicians and campaigns at Substack. “On Substack, there’s a different ethos. Here, a candidate can write to persuade, build a community, and take questions live, all while engaging with voters in a real way. There’s power in that, if candidates take the opportunity. We saw it in this cycle, and I suspect it will be even more pronounced in 2028.”


[Kellianne Jones](https://open.substack.com/users/1990444-kellianne-jones?utm_source=mentions)


, who also works with campaigns at Substack, points to what that means when a candidate has news to break. “Every 2028 campaign should skip the gatekeepers,” she says. “Op-eds need to be pitched and edited and then may run behind a paywall or in an outlet that may come with ideological baggage. On Substack, you hit publish, and it lands directly in your subscribers’ inboxes.”


---


### **A playbook for 2028**


Campaigns have used Substack to communicate in a number of ways: through newsletters, podcasts, live shows, and direct chats with audiences. Here are some best practices to help candidates build a direct line to the people they hope to represent.


**Post Notes regularly**


Candidates use the short-form Notes feed to introduce themselves, share quick updates, and reach readers beyond their existing subscribers.


-


Maryland


[Rep. Jamie Raskin](https://open.substack.com/users/333672972-rep-jamie-raskin?utm_source=mentions)


and Oklahoma Sen.


[Markwayne Mullin](https://open.substack.com/users/439641583-markwayne-mullin?utm_source=mentions)


each used their first Note to say hello and introduce their plans for Substack:


-


Texas Sen.-elect


posted his celebratory Whataburger stop from election night:


-


California Gov.


[Gavin Newsom](https://open.substack.com/users/354255572-gavin-newsom?utm_source=mentions)


posts direct-to-camera video updates straight to Notes.


**Use your first post to make a statement**


Take advantage of the news cycle, or the news you want to break, to time your launch post.


-


Former Vice President


[Kamala Harris](https://open.substack.com/users/386409469-kamala-harris?utm_source=mentions)


launched as her book


*107 Days* was coming out, publishing an excerpt under the title


[“So — what do we do?”](https://kamalaharris.substack.com/p/so-what-do-we-do)


-


North Carolina Sen.-elect


used his first post, “


[Together, we can keep North Carolina moving forward](https://roycoopernc.substack.com/p/together-we-can-keep-north-carolina) ,” to announce his run for U.S. Senate.


**Be personal**


Connecting with the people you represent lets you show them who you are and what you care about.


-


Illinois Gov.


[JB Pritzker](https://open.substack.com/users/268322669-jb-pritzker?utm_source=mentions)


offered


[a personal take](https://jbpritzker.substack.com/p/yes-im-on-it-glp-1s-are-making-people) on his use of GLP-1s.


-


Pennsylvania Gov.


[Josh Shapiro](https://open.substack.com/users/402951427-josh-shapiro?utm_source=mentions)


wrote about the


[arson attack on his home](https://substack.com/@joshshapiropa/p-176183786) .


-


posted


[his summer reading list](https://roycoopernc.substack.com/p/between-stops-a-few-of-the-books) .


**Go live or host videos and podcasts**


Go live on your own channel and with others. You can also


[host and distribute a podcast natively from Substack](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037462092-How-do-I-create-and-publish-a-podcast-on-Substack) or


[cross-post a show hosted elsewhere](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/52072365337620-How-do-I-distribute-my-podcast-to-Substack-if-it-s-hosted-elsewhere) .


-


Former Transportation Secretary


[Pete Buttigieg](https://open.substack.com/users/284251312-pete-buttigieg?utm_source=mentions)


[livestreamed a town hall](https://x.com/adamwren/status/2012334935885951270?s=20) to 13,000 people on Substack.


-


Virginia Sen.


[Mark Warner](https://open.substack.com/users/129762506-mark-warner?utm_source=mentions)


[took extemporaneous questions](https://senatorwarner.substack.com/p/answering-your-questions-live) from his livestream audience.


-


New York Rep.


[Ritchie Torres](https://open.substack.com/users/308455662-ritchie-torres?utm_source=mentions)


sends


[produced videos](https://ritchietorres.substack.com/p/standing-with-nurses?utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web&triedRedirect=true) straight to his subscribers’ inboxes.


-


Kentucky Gov.


[Andy Beshear](https://open.substack.com/users/529196721-andy-beshear?utm_source=mentions)


publishes a


[weekly podcast](https://andybeshear.substack.com/p/democrats-win-big-everywhere-featuring-671) featuring unscripted conversations with leaders, educators, and innovators, and distributes it to YouTube and other platforms.


Partner with creators beyond the usual news and politics circuit, too. Having a conversation with someone from another corner of Substack can bring your perspective to a new audience.


**Open up Chat and answer questions**


Put your most transparent foot forward with AMAs, and let people ask you questions directly. Or do a Q&A in a written post.


-


Ohio Sen.-elect


and Michigan Rep.


[Chairwoman Lisa McClain](https://open.substack.com/users/544065226-chairwoman-lisa-mcclain?utm_source=mentions)


each published a Q&A:


[Sherrod's Substack My answers to your questions Thanks to everyone who sent in a question. This was a great way to spend some time out on the road. Let’s dive in… Read more 19 days ago · 67 likes · 15 comments · Sherrod Brown](https://sherrodbrown.substack.com/p/my-answers-to-your-questions?utm_source=substack&utm_campaign=post_embed&utm_medium=web&embedding_publication_id=1)


[The Commonsense Brief You Asked. I Answered. A few weeks ago, I asked readers of The Common Sense Brief to send me their questions. You did — about AI, Iran, Washington, President Trump, and Congress. Here are your Qs along with my As. Got to as many as I could… Read more a month ago · 59 likes · 22 comments · Chairwoman Lisa McClain](https://commonsensebrief.substack.com/p/you-asked-i-answered?utm_source=substack&utm_campaign=post_embed&utm_medium=web&embedding_publication_id=1)


**Share your Substack**


Announce your Substack to your existing audiences on email and social platforms so that people know they can see more of your thinking and work on Substack.


-


California Rep.


[Sam Liccardo](https://open.substack.com/users/263586831-sam-liccardo?utm_source=mentions)


introduced his new Substack with


[a video on X](https://x.com/sliccardo/status/2075629025402507403?s=20) .


-


Nevada Rep.


[Steven Horsford](https://open.substack.com/users/497408006-steven-horsford?utm_source=mentions)


announced his Substack


[in an official press release](https://horsford.house.gov/media/press-releases/horsford-recently-launches-substack-focused-on-democracy-economic-opportunity-and-public-policy) .


One takeaway from this historic election? “Voters are tired of being talked at. The candidates who did well this year were the ones who connected with people directly,”


notes. “Democrats used Substack to do that this political cycle, and there’s no reason Republicans can’t do the same in the next. Any candidate willing to be open and genuine with voters has a real opportunity to reap the rewards of direct relationships.”


---
